reading:
Microsoft Corporation is a public company trading as MSFT, SEC filer CIK 0000789019, headquartered on its long-standing Redmond, Washington campus. Azure, its cloud computing platform, is the business unit operating the data centers tracked in this registry.

Azure's own geographies page names ten US commercial regions, South Central US, West US, West US 2, West US 3, Central US, East US, East US 2, East US 3, West Central US, and North Central US, plus five separate US government and defense regions, US Gov Virginia, US Gov Arizona, US Gov Texas, US DoD Central, and US DoD East. The page states Azure operates across more than 50 countries and territories worldwide but does not aggregate its regions into a single global count on that page.

The registry here tracks 62 Microsoft facilities across nine states and one US territory, Arizona, California, Iowa, Illinois, Puerto Rico, Texas, Virginia, Washington, and Wyoming. That Microsoft maintains named government-only regions in Virginia, Arizona, and Texas, separate from its commercial regions, points to a deliberate split between commercial cloud infrastructure and government or defense workloads, a distinction not present in the same form in AWS's or Google's public region lists reviewed elsewhere in this registry.

Microsoft's interactive 3D infrastructure map, which is the company's primary public presentation of its global data center footprint, is a JavaScript-rendered application and returned no extractable data this session, so this entry relies on the plain Azure geographies listing instead. No dollar-denominated US investment figure or IT capacity total in megawatts was located this session.
